lessons.title: Directions and Asking for Locations
lessons.body:
When you need to find a place in a Spanish-speaking country, start with 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡...?' (Where is...?). For example, 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ la estaciÃ³n de autobuses?' (Where is the bus station?). If you're asking a stranger, begin with 'Disculpe' (Excuse me). To understand the answer, learn these key words: 'a la derecha' (to the right), 'a la izquierda' (to the left), 'derecho' (straight ahead), 'cerca' (close), 'lejos' (far), 'una cuadra' (one block), 'una esquina' (a corner). In many African cities, landmarks are used instead of street names. So you might hear: 'Siga derecho hasta la farmacia, luego gire a la izquierda en la escuela.' (Go straight until the pharmacy, then turn left at the school.)

Practice asking for directions to common places: 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ el mercado?' (Where is the market?), 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ el banco?' (Where is the bank?), 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ el baÃ±o?' (Where is the bathroom?). If you get lost, say 'Estoy perdido' (I'm lost). To confirm you understood, repeat: 'Entonces, Â¿voy a la derecha?' (So, I go to the right?). Numbers are useful: 'la primera calle' (the first street), 'la segunda calle' (the second street). In rural areas, directions might include 'kilÃ³metro 5' (kilometer 5) or 'junto al rÃ­o' (next to the river).

If you're in a taxi or boda boda, you can say 'LlÃ©veme a...' (Take me to...). For example, 'LlÃ©veme al aeropuerto, por favor.' (Take me to the airport, please.) To ask the driver to stop, say 'Pare aquÃ­' (Stop here). In many African countries, motorbike taxis are common; in Spanish, they might be called 'moto taxis' or 'boda boda' (in Equatorial Guinea). Always agree on the price before you start: 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto cuesta?' (How much does it cost?).

A useful tool is a maps app like Google Maps, but if you don't have data, ask for written directions. Carry a small notebook and ask the person to write it down. Learn to say 'Â¿Puede escribirlo?' (Can you write it down?). Also, learn to read street signs: 'Calle' (Street), 'Avenida' (Avenue), 'Carretera' (Highway). In some countries, addresses include 'barrio' (neighborhood) and 'referencia' (landmark). For example, 'Barrio Centro, frente a la iglesia' (Downtown neighborhood, in front of the church). Practice these phrases with a language partner or by using apps like Duolingo or Babbel. The more you practice, the easier it gets.

lessons.title: Modes of Transport: Taxi, Bus, Boda Boda, Truck
lessons.body:
In Spanish-speaking countries, you'll find many modes of transport. A taxi is 'taxi' or 'libre' (in some places, 'colectivo' for shared taxi). A bus is 'autobÃºs' or 'bus'. In some countries, a minibus is 'micro' or 'combi'. A motorbike taxi is 'moto taxi' or 'boda boda' (in Equatorial Guinea). A truck is 'camiÃ³n'. To ask for a taxi, say 'Â¿DÃ³nde puedo tomar un taxi?' (Where can I take a taxi?). For a bus, 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ la parada de autobÃºs?' (Where is the bus stop?).

When you get in a taxi, confirm the fare: 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto cuesta al centro?' (How much to downtown?). In many African cities, taxis don't use meters, so you must negotiate. Start with 'Â¿Me puede llevar por 5000 francos?' (Can you take me for 5000 francs?). In Latin America, you might say 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto me cobra?' (How much will you charge me?). For buses, you usually pay the conductor: 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto es el pasaje?' (How much is the fare?). Keep small bills and coins handy.

For boda boda, always agree on the price first and ask for a helmet: 'Â¿Tiene casco?' (Do you have a helmet?). In some countries, boda bodas are called 'mototaxis'. To say 'slow down', say 'mÃ¡s despacio'. To say 'stop here', 'pare aquÃ­'. For trucks, if you need to transport goods, say 'Necesito un camiÃ³n para llevar mercancÃ­a' (I need a truck to carry goods). Ask about capacity: 'Â¿CuÃ¡ntas toneladas puede llevar?' (How many tons can it carry?).

If you're traveling between cities, you might take a 'bus interurbano' (intercity bus). Ask for the schedule: 'Â¿A quÃ© hora sale el bus?' (What time does the bus leave?). For long trips, there may be 'bus cama' (sleeper bus) or 'bus ejecutivo' (executive bus). In West Africa, you might find 'sept-place' (seven-seater) taxis. Always keep your luggage with you or get a receipt: 'Â¿Me da un recibo?' (Can you give me a receipt?).

Safety tips: In taxis, sit in the back. For boda boda, hold on tight. For buses, keep your valuables secure. Learn to say 'Voy a bajar en...' (I'm going to get off at...). Also, 'Â¿Me avisa cuando lleguemos?' (Will you let me know when we arrive?). Practice these phrases with a friend or using language apps.

lessons.title: Buying Tickets and Reserving Seats
lessons.body:
Buying tickets in Spanish is straightforward once you know the phrases. For a bus or train ticket, go to the 'taquilla' (ticket window) or 'boleterÃ­a'. Say 'Quiero un boleto a...' (I want a ticket to...). For example, 'Quiero un boleto a Malabo, por favor.' (I want a ticket to Malabo, please.) If you want a round-trip ticket, say 'ida y vuelta'. One-way is 'solo ida'. For multiple tickets, say 'dos boletos' (two tickets).

To reserve a seat, you might say 'Quiero reservar un asiento' (I want to reserve a seat). If you prefer a window seat, 'asiento de ventana'; aisle seat, 'asiento de pasillo'. For a bus, you might ask 'Â¿Puedo elegir mi asiento?' (Can I choose my seat?). In some countries, you can buy tickets online or via mobile money. For example, in Kenya, you can use M-Pesa to pay for bus tickets. In Spanish, 'Puedo pagar con M-Pesa?' (Can I pay with M-Pesa?).

When buying a ticket, you'll need to provide your name and sometimes your ID: 'Â¿Necesita mi identificaciÃ³n?' (Do you need my ID?). For international travel, you'll need a passport: 'AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi pasaporte' (Here is my passport). Ask about luggage: 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto equipaje puedo llevar?' (How much luggage can I bring?). There may be an extra fee for excess luggage: 'Â¿Hay cargo extra por equipaje?' (Is there an extra charge for luggage?).

If you need to change your ticket, say 'Quiero cambiar mi boleto' (I want to change my ticket). For a refund, 'Quiero un reembolso' (I want a refund). Keep your ticket safe; you'll need it to board. At the gate, show your ticket: 'AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi boleto' (Here is my ticket). The conductor might ask 'Â¿A dÃ³nde va?' (Where are you going?). Answer clearly.

Useful vocabulary: 'andÃ©n' (platform), 'salida' (departure), 'llegada' (arrival), 'retraso' (delay), 'cancelado' (cancelled). If there's a delay, ask 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto tiempo de retraso?' (How long is the delay?). Practice buying tickets with a language partner or using apps like Duolingo. In real life, start with simple transactions at local bus stations.

lessons.title: Talking About Delivery Times and Routes
lessons.body:
If you're in logistics, you'll need to discuss delivery times and routes. Start with 'Â¿CuÃ¡ndo es la entrega?' (When is the delivery?). To say 'The delivery is tomorrow', 'La entrega es maÃ±ana'. For a specific time, 'La entrega es a las 3 de la tarde' (The delivery is at 3 PM). If you need to delay, 'Necesito posponer la entrega' (I need to postpone the delivery). To confirm, 'Â¿Puede entregar el lunes?' (Can you deliver on Monday?).

For routes, ask 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es la ruta?' (What is the route?). To describe a route, use 'pasar por' (to pass through), 'llegar a' (to arrive at), 'salir de' (to leave from). For example, 'Salimos de Accra, pasamos por LomÃ©, y llegamos a CotonÃº' (We leave from Accra, pass through LomÃ©, and arrive in Cotonou). If there's a toll, 'peaje'; a border, 'frontera'. Ask 'Â¿Hay peajes en la ruta?' (Are there tolls on the route?).

Delivery times can be affected by traffic, weather, or customs. Say 'El trÃ¡fico estÃ¡ pesado' (Traffic is heavy). 'Hay mucha lluvia' (There's a lot of rain). 'La aduana estÃ¡ lenta' (Customs is slow). To give an estimate, 'La entrega tomarÃ¡ 3 horas' (The delivery will take 3 hours). If you're late, 'Lo siento, voy retrasado' (Sorry, I'm running late).

For tracking, you might say 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ el camiÃ³n?' (Where is the truck?). 'El conductor estÃ¡ en la frontera' (The driver is at the border). Use numbers: 'kilÃ³metros' (kilometers), 'horas' (hours), 'dÃ­as' (days). For example, 'La distancia es 200 kilÃ³metros' (The distance is 200 kilometers). 'El viaje dura 4 horas' (The trip takes 4 hours).

If you need to change the route, 'Necesitamos cambiar la ruta' (We need to change the route). Ask for alternatives: 'Â¿Hay otra ruta?' (Is there another route?). In case of breakdown, 'El camiÃ³n se descompuso' (The truck broke down). 'Necesitamos un mecÃ¡nico' (We need a mechanic). Practice these phrases with a colleague or using language apps. In real logistics, clear communication saves time and money.

lessons.title: Customs and Border Crossing Phrases
lessons.body:
Crossing borders in Africa often involves customs checks. Learn key phrases to make it smoother. At the border, you'll see 'Aduana' (Customs) and 'MigraciÃ³n' (Immigration). Have your documents ready: 'AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi pasaporte' (Here is my passport). 'AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi visa' (Here is my visa). If you're transporting goods, you'll need a 'declaraciÃ³n de aduana' (customs declaration). Say 'Tengo mercancÃ­a para declarar' (I have goods to declare).

The officer may ask 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es el propÃ³sito de su viaje?' (What is the purpose of your trip?). Answer 'Negocios' (Business) or 'Turismo' (Tourism). For goods, 'Â¿QuÃ© lleva?' (What are you carrying?). Answer 'Llevo productos electrÃ³nicos' (I'm carrying electronics). If you have nothing to declare, 'No tengo nada que declarar' (I have nothing to declare).

You might need to pay duties: 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto tengo que pagar?' (How much do I have to pay?). Ask for a receipt: 'Â¿Me da un recibo?' (Can you give me a receipt?). If there's a delay, 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto tiempo toma?' (How long does it take?). For inspections, 'Â¿Puede revisar mi equipaje?' (Can you check my luggage?).

In some borders, you might need a yellow fever certificate: 'AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi certificado de fiebre amarilla' (Here is my yellow fever certificate). For vehicles, you need 'permiso de circulaciÃ³n' (circulation permit) and 'seguro' (insurance). Say 'Tengo el seguro del vehÃ­culo' (I have vehicle insurance). If you're a driver, 'Soy el conductor' (I am the driver).

If you face issues, stay calm and polite. 'Disculpe, no entiendo' (Excuse me, I don't understand). 'Â¿Puede hablar mÃ¡s despacio?' (Can you speak slower?). 'Â¿Hay un intÃ©rprete?' (Is there an interpreter?). Useful words: 'frontera' (border), 'control' (checkpoint), 'documentos' (documents), 'impuesto' (tax). Practice these phrases with a language partner. Knowing them can save you hours at the border.

lessons.title: Practice: Plan a Delivery Route in Spanish
lessons.body:
Now let's put everything together. You'll plan a delivery route from Accra, Ghana to Lagos, Nigeria, using Spanish. First, gather your team and say: 'Vamos a planificar la ruta de entrega' (Let's plan the delivery route). Start by identifying the origin and destination: 'Salimos de Accra y llegamos a Lagos' (We leave from Accra and arrive in Lagos). The distance is about 1,000 kilometers. 'La distancia es mil kilÃ³metros' (The distance is 1,000 kilometers).

Next, choose the mode of transport. For goods, you'll use a truck: 'Usamos un camiÃ³n' (We use a truck). Ask about capacity: 'Â¿CuÃ¡ntas toneladas puede llevar el camiÃ³n?' (How many tons can the truck carry?). Suppose it's 10 tons: 'Puede llevar 10 toneladas' (It can carry 10 tons). Plan the route: 'La ruta pasa por LomÃ©, CotonÃº, y Porto-Novo' (The route passes through LomÃ©, Cotonou, and Porto-Novo). There are border crossings: 'Hay tres fronteras' (There are three borders).

Estimate delivery time: 'El viaje dura 3 dÃ­as' (The trip takes 3 days). But consider delays: 'Puede haber retrasos en la aduana' (There may be delays at customs). So, 'La entrega serÃ¡ el viernes' (The delivery will be on Friday). Communicate with the driver: 'Conductor, Â¿dÃ³nde estÃ¡ ahora?' (Driver, where are you now?). 'Estoy en la frontera de Togo' (I'm at the Togo border).

Prepare documents: 'Necesitamos pasaportes, visas, y declaraciones de aduana' (We need passports, visas, and customs declarations). For the truck: 'Necesitamos permiso de circulaciÃ³n y seguro' (We need circulation permit and insurance). If there's a breakdown: 'El camiÃ³n se descompuso en Benin' (The truck broke down in Benin). 'Necesitamos un mecÃ¡nico' (We need a mechanic).

Finally, confirm the delivery: 'La entrega fue exitosa' (The delivery was successful). 'El cliente recibiÃ³ la mercancÃ­a' (The client received the goods). Practice this scenario with a partner. Use a map and speak only Spanish. This will build your confidence for real logistics work.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Navigating Transport and Logistics in Spanish-Speaking Africa

For African agribusiness professionals moving goods and people across Spanish-speaking markets â Equatorial Guinea, and trade corridors linking to Spanish-speaking partners â fluent logistics Spanish is a commercial advantage. This Practical Reference consolidates the vocabulary, phrases, and operational frameworks you need to move cargo, negotiate transport, clear borders, and plan delivery routes with confidence. Whether you are arranging a truck from Malabo to Bata, booking a boda boda for last-mile distribution in a farming community, or negotiating customs at the CameroonâEquatorial Guinea border, the language you use determines your speed, cost, and margin.

This lesson is business-first: every phrase is framed for commercial use. You will find ready-to-use expressions for directions, transport modes, ticketing, delivery scheduling, and customs. The reference tables, diagram, and checklist are designed to be printed or saved for field use.

1. Directions and Asking for Locations

When you arrive in a new market town, the first task is orientation. Spanish direction phrases are direct and practical. Use formal address (usted) with officials and elders; informal (tÃº) with drivers and market traders once rapport is established.

  • Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ el mercado central? â Where is the central market?
  • Â¿CÃ³mo llego al puerto / a la aduana? â How do I get to the port / customs?
  • Siga recto, luego gire a la derecha / izquierda. â Go straight, then turn right / left.
  • EstÃ¡ a dos kilÃ³metros, pasando el cruce. â It is two kilometres away, past the junction.
  • Â¿EstÃ¡ lejos de aquÃ­? â Is it far from here?
  • El almacÃ©n estÃ¡ detrÃ¡s de la estaciÃ³n de servicio. â The warehouse is behind the fuel station.

In Equatorial Guinea, major commercial hubs include Malabo (Bioko Island), Bata (mainland), and EbebiyÃ­n (near the Cameroon and Gabon borders). Knowing how to ask for these locations precisely saves hours. For agribusiness, the key destinations are ports, customs offices, wholesale markets, and rural collection points.

2. Modes of Transport: Taxi, Bus, Boda Boda, Truck

Choosing the right transport mode is a costâspeedârisk decision. In Equatorial Guinea and neighbouring corridors, the main options are:

Table 1: Transport modes for agribusiness logistics in Spanish-speaking Africa
Mode Spanish Term Best Use Typical Cost Indicator Risk Note
Taxi Taxi / coche de alquiler Urban meetings, small samples, airport transfers Negotiate before boarding; shared taxis cheaper Meter rarely used; agree price first
Bus AutobÃºs / guagua Intercity travel, small cargo in luggage hold Fixed fare; buy at station Limited cargo capacity; schedule delays
Boda Boda Moto-taxi / boda boda Last-mile delivery, rural collection points Per trip; negotiate in local currency Weather exposure; cargo security
Truck CamiÃ³n / camioneta Bulk agricultural produce, cross-border freight Per tonne-km; fuel surcharge Customs delays; road conditions

Cost indicators are directional only. Verify current rates with local freight forwarders. Source: World Bank Transport Practice, 2023.

Useful phrases:

  • Necesito un camiÃ³n de cinco toneladas para llevar cafÃ© a Bata. â I need a five-tonne truck to take coffee to Bata.
  • Â¿CuÃ¡nto cobra por el viaje a EbebiyÃ­n? â How much do you charge for the trip to EbebiyÃ­n?
  • Â¿La boda boda puede llevar dos sacos de maÃ­z? â Can the moto-taxi carry two sacks of maize?
  • El autobÃºs sale a las seis de la maÃ±ana. â The bus leaves at six in the morning.

3. Buying Tickets and Reserving Seats

Ticket transactions are a test of clarity. Always confirm departure time, platform, luggage allowance, and refund policy in Spanish.

  • Quisiera reservar dos asientos para el autobÃºs de las 7:00. â I would like to reserve two seats for the 7:00 bus.
  • Â¿CuÃ¡nto equipaje puedo llevar? â How much luggage can I bring?
  • Â¿Hay descuento por compra de ida y vuelta? â Is there a discount for a return ticket?
  • Â¿Puedo cambiar la fecha del billete? â Can I change the ticket date?
  • Un billete de ida a Bata, por favor. â A one-way ticket to Bata, please.
Table 2: Essential ticketing and reservation vocabulary
Spanish English Business Context
Billete / boleto Ticket Bus, ferry, train
Asiento Seat Reservation confirmation
Ida y vuelta Round trip Cost negotiation
Salida / llegada Departure / arrival Schedule planning
Equipaje Luggage Cargo allowance
Factura Invoice / receipt Expense reporting

Vocabulary verified against Instituto Cervantes Spanish language resources and regional usage in Equatorial Guinea.

4. Talking About Delivery Times and Routes

Delivery commitments are contractual. Use precise time expressions and route descriptions.

  • La entrega estÃ¡ prevista para el viernes a las 14:00. â Delivery is scheduled for Friday at 14:00.
  • El camiÃ³n saldrÃ¡ de Malabo a las 5:00 y llegarÃ¡ a Bata en ocho horas. â The truck will leave Malabo at 5:00 and arrive in Bata in eight hours.
  • La ruta pasa por EbebiyÃ­n; hay un control aduanero. â The route goes through EbebiyÃ­n; there is a customs checkpoint.
  • Â¿CuÃ¡l es el tiempo de trÃ¡nsito habitual? â What is the usual transit time?
  • Hay retrasos por lluvia en la carretera. â There are delays due to rain on the road.

In agribusiness, perishability matters. Always ask about cold chain availability: Â¿El camiÃ³n tiene refrigeraciÃ³n? (Does the truck have refrigeration?). For export crops like cocoa, coffee, and rubber, coordinate with the buyer on arrival windows.

5. Customs and Border Crossing Phrases

Border crossings in Central Africa can be slow. Prepared documentation and clear Spanish speed the process.

  • AquÃ­ estÃ¡ la declaraciÃ³n de aduanas. â Here is the customs declaration.
  • Llevo productos agrÃ­colas para exportaciÃ³n. â I am carrying agricultural products for export.
  • Â¿Necesito un certificado fitosanitario? â Do I need a phytosanitary certificate?
  • Â¿CuÃ¡nto es el arancel de importaciÃ³n? â How much is the import duty?
  • El contenedor estÃ¡ sellado y precintado. â The container is sealed and stamped.
  • Â¿Puedo hablar con el oficial de aduanas? â Can I speak with the customs officer?
â  SAFETY WARNING â Customs and Border Compliance

Never attempt to cross a border without complete documentation. Undeclared agricultural goods can be confiscated, and penalties may include fines or detention. In Equatorial Guinea and neighbouring countries, phytosanitary certificates, export permits, and customs declarations are mandatory for commercial agricultural shipments. Verify requirements with the destination country's embassy or trade ministry before loading cargo. Do not offer or accept unofficial payments; use official channels and keep receipts. Source: WTO Trade Policy Review, Central Africa.

6. Practice: Plan a Delivery Route in Spanish

Apply the module by planning a route from a farm collection point to an urban market. Use the template below and write your plan in Spanish.

Template:

  1. Origen: Finca en [localidad].
  2. Destino: Mercado de [ciudad].
  3. Modo de transporte: CamiÃ³n / boda boda / autobÃºs.
  4. Ruta: Salida a las [hora], pasando por [punto intermedio].
  5. Aduana: Documentos necesarios: [lista].
  6. Tiempo estimado: [horas / dÃ­as].
  7. Presupuesto: [coste estimado].

Example: La entrega sale de la finca en Mongomo a las 4:00. El camiÃ³n de tres toneladas lleva 60 sacos de cacao a Bata. La ruta pasa por EbebiyÃ­n, donde presentamos la declaraciÃ³n de aduanas y el certificado fitosanitario. El tiempo estimado es de seis horas. El coste es de 250.000 francos CFA.

Quick Reference Checklist

  • â Confirm destination and route in Spanish before departure.
  • â Negotiate transport price and confirm in writing (receipt or message).
  • â Verify ticket, seat, and luggage allowance for bus or ferry.
  • â Check delivery time window and cold chain requirements.
  • â Prepare customs documents: declaration, phytosanitary certificate, export permit.
  • â Keep official receipts for all border payments.
  • â Share route and ETA with buyer and local contact.
  • â Have emergency contacts for freight forwarder and customs broker.

Further Reading

  • African Development Bank â Central Africa Transport Corridors
  • World Bank â Transport Practice
  • WTO â Trade Policy Reviews (Central Africa)
  • Instituto Cervantes â Spanish Language Resources
  • FAO Africa â Agricultural Trade and Logistics
